questions.q: Why can't a plain LC oscillator (capacitor + ordinary inductor) be used directly as a qubit?
options: LC oscillators have no energy levels at all
LC oscillators cannot be built on a chip using lithography
LC oscillators only work at room temperature, not at millikelvin temperatures
Its energy levels are evenly spaced, so a microwave pulse tuned to the 0->1 transition would also drive 1->2, 2->3, and higher transitions, making it impossible to isolate a clean two-level system
questions.explain: A linear LC oscillator's quantum energy levels are equally spaced like rungs on a ladder, so there is no way to address only the bottom two levels without also driving transitions higher up -- that's exactly the problem the Josephson junction's nonlinearity solves.

questions.q: What role does the Josephson junction play in a superconducting qubit circuit?
options: It cools the chip down to millikelvin temperatures
It acts as a perfect insulator that blocks all current, isolating the qubit from the rest of the chip
It acts as a nonlinear inductor, which makes the circuit's energy levels unevenly spaced (anharmonic) so a clean two-level system can be isolated
It generates the microwave pulses used to drive the qubit
questions.explain: The Josephson junction's current-dependent, nonlinear inductance is what turns an otherwise evenly-spaced LC oscillator into an anharmonic circuit whose bottom two levels can be treated as an isolated qubit.

questions.q: What does 'anharmonicity' refer to in a superconducting qubit circuit?
options: The physical size difference between the capacitor and the Josephson junction
The number of Cooper pairs tunneling through the junction per second
The amount of electrical resistance remaining in the superconducting wiring
The difference between the 0->1 and 1->2 transition frequencies of the circuit's energy levels
questions.explain: Anharmonicity is specifically the mismatch between adjacent transition frequencies -- it's what allows a microwave pulse to selectively address the 0->1 transition without also driving 1->2.

questions.q: How is the state of a superconducting qubit (|0> or |1>) actually measured?
options: By directly photographing the qubit with an electron microscope while it operates
By weighing the chip before and after the measurement
By measuring the DC voltage across the Josephson junction with a standard voltmeter
Indirectly: the qubit is coupled to a microwave resonator, and the resonator's response to a probe tone shifts depending on the qubit's state, which is what gets measured and amplified off-chip
questions.explain: Readout is never a direct observation of the qubit state -- it's inferred from how the qubit's state perturbs a coupled microwave resonator's reflected or transmitted signal, which is then amplified and digitized.

questions.q: Why must superconducting qubit chips be cooled to temperatures where the circuit material becomes superconducting?
options: Without superconductivity, the circuit has electrical resistance and dissipates energy too quickly to sustain a coherent quantum state
Superconductivity is only needed to make the chip's wiring visible under a microscope
Cooling is purely a cost-saving measure and has no effect on qubit function
Superconductivity increases the anharmonicity of an LC oscillator without needing a Josephson junction
questions.explain: Superconductivity (zero electrical resistance) is the precondition that lets current flow as a coherent quantum wave rather than dissipating as noisy classical current -- without it the circuit behaves classically and loses its quantum state almost immediately.
